skills.title: Different Types of Families
skills.description: Families come in many kinds, like one parent, two parents, blended, foster, or many generations living together. Match each family to its type.

skills.title: Comparing Families and Traditions
skills.description: Families can be alike and different in who is in them, the foods they eat, and the celebrations they have. Sort what is the same and what is different.

skills.title: Family Traditions Over Time
skills.description: Traditions can stay the same or change as families grow. Pick reasons why, like moving to Canada or new technology.

skills.title: Groups in Our Community
skills.description: Our community has many groups, like different cultures, religions, and First Nations, Métis, and Inuit people. Match each group to ways our community shows this, like foods, music, and languages.

skills.title: Traditions and Celebrations
skills.description: Families and communities celebrate days like Diwali, Eid al-Fitr, Canada Day, and Remembrance Day. Match each celebration to who celebrates it and why.

skills.title: Family Events in Order
skills.description: Family events like births, moves, and weddings happen across many generations. Put them in order on a timeline or family tree.

skills.title: Heritage in Community Events
skills.description: Festivals and community events pass on heritage through food, clothing, music, dance, and stories. Pick how each event shares its heritage.

skills.title: Heritage in Family Practices
skills.description: Families pass on heritage through special meals, ceremonies, and growing-up traditions, including First Nations, Métis, and Inuit ones. Match each practice to how it shares heritage.

skills.title: Past and Present Traditions
skills.description: Some traditions in our community were once outlawed or given up, and some have changed. Pick how past and present traditions differ and why.

skills.title: Bringing Traditions Back
skills.description: Settlement and residential schools banned many First Nations, Métis, and Inuit traditions. Pick the ways people are bringing back songs, dances, ceremonies, and clothing.

skills.title: Globes and World Maps
skills.description: The world can be shown on a globe or on print and digital maps. Pick what countries, continents, and water look like on each.

skills.title: Continents, Oceans, Equator, Poles
skills.description: Label the seven continents, the oceans, the equator, the poles, and the hemispheres on a globe or map.

skills.title: North, South, East, West
skills.description: Maps use N, S, E, and W to show direction. Pick where a place is from another place using these directions.

skills.title: Places That Matter to Families
skills.description: Families have special places or countries, like where they came from. Find these places on a globe or map.

skills.title: Where a Place Is and Its Climate
skills.description: Places near the equator are warmer, and places farther north are colder. Match places, including a First Nation, Métis, or Inuit community, to their climate.

skills.title: Reading Photos and Maps
skills.description: Photos and maps give clues about a place, like how warm it is and what the land looks like. Pick the facts you can tell from them.

skills.title: Basic Human Needs
skills.description: People everywhere need food, water, clothing, shelter, and transportation. Match each need to the different ways people around the world meet it.

skills.title: Communities Around the World
skills.description: Communities around the world have different land, animals, houses, and culture, including a First Nation, Métis, or Inuit community. Match each community to what it is like.

skills.title: Comparing Communities
skills.description: Our community and ones far away can be alike or different in homes, food, clothes, and fun. Sort what is the same and what is different.

skills.title: Adapting to Climate and Land
skills.description: People change how they live to fit the weather and land where they are. Match each place to the clothes, homes, or schedules that fit it.

skills.title: Using Nature Carefully
skills.description: If people use water, soil, and animals carefully, there is enough for the future. Pick what happens when people use them wisely and when they do not.
